blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout forever) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Unbounded retry loop with fixed one-second delay, including on permanent errors) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Retrying a non-idempotent charge can charge the customer twice) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`. Without it, when the provider accepts the connection but stops answering, `charge()` blocks indefinitely: the checkout request and its worker hang with no error and no log, and the operator only sees stuck workers. Treat a read timeout as an ambiguous outcome (the charge may have gone through), see R-ops-3.
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout and can hang the checkout forever

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a small maximum number of attempts) with exponential backoff and jitter, then raise. As written, `raise_for_status()` turns a 4xx (declined card, invalid amount, bad credentials) into `requests.HTTPError`, a `RequestException`, so a request that can never succeed is retried every second forever: `charge()` never returns, and during a provider outage every checkout hammers the provider once a second (retry storm). Retry only transient failures (connection errors, 5xx, 429) and surface the others to the caller.
findings.title: Unbounded retry loop with fixed one-second delay, including on permanent errors

findings.recommendation: Make the retried request idempotent: send an idempotency key derived from `order_id` (e.g. an `Idempotency-Key` header, if the provider supports it) so the provider deduplicates repeats, or do not retry an ambiguous outcome. Scenario: the provider processes the charge but the response is lost (connection reset, 502 from a proxy, or a timeout once R-ops-1 is fixed); the `except` branch sleeps and POSTs the same charge again, creating a second charge for the same order.
findings.title: Retrying a non-idempotent charge can charge the customer twice

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt with structured fields (order_id, attempt number, HTTP status, exception type; never the request body or credentials) and raise an actionable error naming the order and the provider status when retries are exhausted. Today, when the provider rejects or fails a charge, the exception is dropped: no log, no metric, no error reaches the caller, so an operator investigating a stuck or unpaid order has nothing to diagnose it with.
findings.title: Payment failures are swallowed without any log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or the project's configuration. The endpoint differs between environments (provider sandbox vs production); with it baked in, a development or staging deployment that calls `charge()` hits the production endpoint, and pointing an environment elsewhere requires a code change and a release.
findings.title: Provider URL hard-coded instead of read from configuration
